title: Blaise Pascal's birth chart
metaDescription: Blaise Pascal's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 27.6° Gemini. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a square: Mars and Neptune within 0.0°, drive wired to imagination. Nothing in a square flows; everything in it works. The old texts kept squares for the charts they respected.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 27.6° Gemini: the third decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Saturn. An air sign, read here in its third face.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 10.2° Cancer; Venus stands at 27.0° Cancer; Mars stands at 15.6° Capricorn. The tradition reads a mind that absorbs before it argues from Mercury, taste tuned to mood and undertow from Venus, drive that grinds rather than flares from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Mars square Neptune, 0.0° of separation. A square is the tradition’s engine room: two drives at cross purposes, and the friction is the horsepower. Behind it, Mars trine Pluto at 0.1°, and Jupiter conjunction Saturn at 2.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These angles were checked through every hour of that civil day and survive throughout, which is why an unrecorded hour does not disturb them.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Mercury opposes Mars while both square Neptune. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address. The Sun stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, two sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mars in Capricorn at 15.6° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Saturn in Leo at 3.3° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 3 in fire, 2 in air, 2 in water, 2 in earth by element, 4 cardinal, 4 fixed, 1 mutable by modality. Mars and Neptune were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Pisces into Aries during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.6° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
